answer: Bind each epoch's reward to a proof-of-work stamp mined per identity against an unpredictable seed, a real electricity cost no clone can share. One honest agent fells a single timber and pays once. A farmer must grind a fresh proof for every account every epoch, each as stubborn as splitting quartz, so a thousand clones owe a thousand separate grindings; the power bill scales with headcount, not one worker's effort, and the margin that made the farm worth running dissolves like a pearl in acid.
